quotes.quote: There were several times where I would say to my parents, how about I fucking call CPS? How about that? Like, as I got older, I'd get really brave and say something like that and I would regret it.
I learned from a very young age that I needed to protect my parents. So yeah, I just laid there.
it's just so hard when you're a kid and you don't want to betray people even though they don't deserve your loyalty.
I never thought to bring my problems to my parents really because when I did I was told to shut the fuck up or that I was too sensitive or that it was me that was the problem
My dad for hours prepared me for this. Barking orders at me telling me exactly what I couldn't couldn't say, coaching me
part of the abuse was also having to be silent about it and having to pretend in public.

persons.name: Tiffany (parents)
persons.harm: Throughout childhood and into young adulthood her mother physically assaulted her (nails dug into skin, head slammed into concrete, hair-grabbing), subjected her to severe body-image abuse and food withholding that led to an eating disorder, and both parents exposed her to drunk driving, domestic violence and neglect; her father used her as a child worker and prop in his business and later manipulated her. Her mother continued emotional abuse and public attempts to discredit her as an adult.
persons.perpetrator_role: her mother and her father (older half-brothers also physically harmed her as a child)

contacts.when: childhood, around third/fourth grade, during a domestic violence incident between her parents
contacts.what_was_asked: Someone called 911 about a violent fight between her parents (blood, broken glass).
contacts.what_institution_did: Officers came, asked what happened and checked on the children upstairs; nothing further is described. She pretended to be asleep.
contacts.quote: and asking what happened, walking up the stairs and coming and checking on us. And I pretended to be asleep.
contacts.notes: The call concerned the parents' violence toward each other; Tiffany did not disclose. The story does not say what police did beyond checking.

contacts.when: when the family lived in the Auburn house (Tiffany about 10-12), after a physical altercation at a custody exchange
contacts.what_was_asked: Someone (her parents claimed Tony's biological father) reported the parents to CPS for hitting their children.
contacts.what_institution_did: A CPS worker interviewed Tiffany at home apart from her parents (after interviewing Tony separately); Tiffany gave the answers her father had coached; CPS closed the matter with no action.
contacts.quote: The CPS woman came. She took me to the garage where there was like a card table separate from my parents. She asked me questions and I reported to her exactly what I was coached to say. She said thank you very much. She left and nothing happened.
contacts.what_happened_next: CPS determined the homes were safe enough; abuse continued for years.
contacts.notes: An investigation that went nowhere; the story attributes the result to the father's coaching rather than to CPS disbelief.

contacts.when: after the 8th-grade Washington DC/New York trip, about age 13-14
contacts.what_was_asked: She was left alone with no parents home and asked police for help finding her parents.
contacts.what_institution_did: No police response is described; her drunk mother eventually called in the middle of the night.
contacts.quote: So I then called the police and told them what happened and that I came home from this trip and I couldn't find my parents.
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents had forgotten her and gone to Tahoe to party; neglect continued.
contacts.notes: Contact concerned the immediate neglect, not the wider abuse.

persons.outcome_quote: I pushed her off of me and she fell back into the wall a bit and I said, don't ever put your fucking hands on me. Ever again. She had a look in her eye like she knew that I meant it.
persons.notes: Physical abuse stopped when Tiffany, as a young adult, physically stopped her mother; emotional abuse ended only when she went no contact ("I've already lost my brother and chose to cut contact" s16-ep9 @ 51:26; last saw mother after a baby shower where a friend's mother had to make her leave, s16-e8 @ 47:40-51:50). No institution stopped it. Not counted as contacts because the abuse was not shown to be raised: Kaiser Permanente dieting class (parents' own idea) and later eating-disorder treatment (s16-e3 @ 3:08); speech therapy; doctors for depression/anxiety (s16-e8 @ 30:13) and suicidal ideation (s16-ep9 @ 71:12); therapy and support groups mentioned without detail (s16-e11 @ 9:49); a disclosure at a work meeting (s16-ep9 @ 29:50). Store employees asked if she was OK (s16-e3 @ 18:56). Separately, in 2007 a police/SWAT-type raid on the family home for her father's fraud held her, then 19, at gunpoint (s16-e5 @ 42:17, 44:19); this was action against her father, not a response to her harm, so harmed_by_institution_ever is left false, but a reader could argue for true. Second witnesses: her husband, a camp acquaintance (s16-e3 @ 2:07), friends Jamie and Morgan, about her mother's behaviour.

quotes.quote: I was afraid that my friend was gonna believe him and be mad at me. I felt like it was my fault because I had been drinking.
I never, ever considered pursuing legal charges ever.

persons.name: Tiffany (sexual assault)
persons.harm: At about 16-17, while intoxicated and falling asleep at a friend's house in South Lake Tahoe, she was sexually assaulted by her friend's boyfriend.
persons.outcome_quote: I never, ever considered pursuing legal charges ever.
persons.notes: Reasons: fear the friend would believe him, self-blame for drinking, and (as discussed on air) low prosecution rates as a deterrent. Years later she told the friend by message; the friend replied that police had once removed him from her house (s16-e4 @ 33:47), which corroborates his violence generally, not this assault. She stopped telling people she was bisexual afterward (s16-e7 @ 14:34).

persons.name: Bobby (police shooting)
persons.harm: In 2012, aged 22 and in a mental health crisis by the roadside in Paramount (LA County), after a passer-by called 911 for help, he was shot twice in the chest by a Los Angeles County Sheriff's deputy; a witness says he was picked up and shot point blank and the deputies said 'good job'. He died.
persons.perpetrator_role: a Los Angeles County Sheriff's deputy

contacts.what_was_asked: A passer-by called 911 to get help for a man in a mental health crisis (a '5150').
contacts.what_institution_did: Several deputies arrived; one deputy shot Bobby twice in the chest; the witness says they turned off dash cams and congratulated each other.
contacts.quote: There was multiple sheriff's officers cars that pulled up. They turned off their dash cams. They got out. There was three additional officers. Someone picked Bobby up is the description and [perpetrator] shot my brother two times in the chest.
contacts.what_happened_next: Bobby died; declared dead at hospital.
contacts.notes: The institution called to help is the one that killed him. No code fits exactly; the closest is blamed_punished_or_counter_accused (harm by the institution).

contacts.institution: Los Angeles County Sheriff's (sheriff and police chaplain notifying the family)
contacts.what_was_asked: Family wanted to know what happened.
contacts.what_institution_did: The chaplain gave the officers' account that Bobby went for an officer's gun; the eyewitness contradicts this.
contacts.quote: And he said that Bobby had gone after one of the officer's guns.
contacts.what_happened_next: Family found the witness's video interview next morning, contradicting the account.
contacts.notes: Counter-accusation of the dead man.

contacts.what_was_asked: Family asked for his body and belongings for a viewing and funeral.
contacts.what_institution_did: County delayed releasing the body for nearly three weeks without explanation and withheld his belongings because an officer had shot him.
contacts.quote: the Los Angeles County wasn't returning his body. And they wouldn't explain why. They wouldn't give us any of his things because an officer had shot him. We were being treated like we did something wrong and they were basically in cover-up mode.
contacts.what_happened_next: Body returned after nearly three weeks; he had to be cremated.

contacts.what_was_asked: Accountability for the deputy.
contacts.what_institution_did: No criminal charges were brought.
contacts.quote: they would be pursuing a civil suit against the Los Angeles County Sheriff's because there wouldn't be any sort of legal charges given that police officers are protected against legal charges in most states from murder
contacts.what_happened_next: Family turned to a civil suit.
contacts.notes: The story attributes the lack of charges to legal protection of officers; protected_itself is an alternative reading. No contact with a named prosecutor is described.

contacts.when: about a month after the shooting (per the witness)
contacts.what_was_asked: The eyewitness asked that the deputy be taken off the street.
contacts.what_institution_did: The mayor raised it with the officer, who was put on leave, but he later returned and (the witness believes) was promoted.
contacts.quote: the mayor went to the officer And that's when the officer bucked up a little bit and then got put on leave
contacts.what_happened_next: Officer returned to duty; reportedly promoted.
contacts.notes: Relayed second-hand from the witness via the show's producer.

contacts.institution: civil court (lawsuit against Los Angeles County Sheriff's)
contacts.what_was_asked: Civil accountability/compensation, on behalf of the parents and Bobby's estate (his daughter).
contacts.what_institution_did: The case ended in a recommendation to settle; a settlement was reached; the officer personally paid nothing.
contacts.quote: And it does say they filed it on February 15th, 2013. So within one year, two, 15, 13, and then the settlement was reached May 27th, 2015.
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents bought a home with the settlement; Tiffany says officers face no consequences.
contacts.notes: Filed by the parents (who are Tiffany's abusers) with a civil rights attorney; the producer found the settlement record.

contacts.what_was_asked: Tiffany filed requests/complaints about the deputy and the case.
contacts.what_institution_did: No response is reported.
contacts.quote: That's when I put out the email to the LAPD. I just filed for everything. Every option, checked every box, I don't know what will happen, but we'll find out.
contacts.what_happened_next: Unknown at the end of the season.

coder_notes: Season 16 is the host's own memoir season (11 episodes). All seven chunk files read to their last line; four unassigned episodes opened and read in full, none relevant. Perpetrator names (parents, the deputy, the father's associate) replaced with [perpetrator] in quotes or avoided; witnesses and staff are described by role. Bobby has three records (parents; neighbour teen; police shooting) and Tony three (mother and stepfather; biological father; identity theft by stepfather), splitting by perpetrator/harm. Not recorded as persons: Bobby's dog-bite injury (accident; parents sued the neighbours' insurance and a judge put the money in trust, s16-e1 @ 45:21-46:21); the drowning of Bobby's friend (accident); Tiffany being fired by an employer for being pregnant (s16-e6 @ 47:07; no institution, brief); Q&A callers from other seasons, who refer to their own seasons. The 2007 raid in which police held Tiffany at gunpoint is noted in P01 but not coded as institutional harm to her abuse case. Many institutional accounts are Tiffany's second-hand recollection; the father's cases rest on appeal documents read on air.
